text:
marco: heads up — between 03:12 and 03:25 UTC we saw ~60 GPU pod evictions across eu-west1 during the nightly randomized drain run. lots of reschedules into other AZs, egress spikes, and a couple of model-serving tails blown past SLO. suspecting lease fragmentation on the shard pools + descheduler churn :rotating_light:

sasha: ugh. can you paste the eviction events? were these preemptive taints or normal node drains?

marco: paste from node-events log:```
I0312 03:13:01.123 kubelet eviction manager: evicting pod model-x (priority=900) due to signal: NoResources (gpu_fraction unavailable)
I0312 03:13:01.456 scheduler: binding model-x -> node-gpu-12 (az-b)
I0312 03:13:05.789 descheduler: removed pod model-x from node-gpu-11 to reduce fragmentation
```
Not taint-based. It's the randomized drain job that picks nodes to defrag, plus the lease allocator is returning many tiny leases which leads scheduler to scatter replicas.

oncall-bot: ALERT: bulk-eviction-detected (threshold=50) — channel eng-platform notified.

elin: timeline matches a change to lease TTL we rolled last week (shorter TTL to free transient capacity). That made leases expire more often and the defrag job now sees many small free ranges.

kim: short TTL makes sense for bursty infra but combined with randomized drains is bad. two immediate proposals: 1) increase lease TTL for shard pools to 30m, 2) add a jitter window so randomized drains don't overlap across AZs.

raj: quick ops note — autoscaler scale-down is currently 5m. when nodes are drained and pods reschedule we trigger scale-up in other AZs which then gets throttled and creates more churn. bumping scale-down to 15m would reduce flare. also we should mark smaller inference replicas with a soft-affinity so they pack better.

marco: agree on scale-down. also we should try "lease coalescing" in the allocator: coalesce adjacent tiny free leases into larger contiguous chunks before handing out. That would let the scheduler place multi-GPU jobs on single node instead of scattering.

sasha: implementation-wise coalescing is straightforward. but need to be careful with race conditions. propose a quick mitigation: make randomized-drain run with a per-AZ semaphore and a 10m cooldown so only one drain runs in an AZ at a time. low-risk and fast.

elin: also seen network egress spike because cross-AZ reschedules cause model shards to pull large checkpoints during cold start. we should prefer keeping existing KV cache in place by honoring pod affinity for shard owners. maybe add a "sticky-shard" soft-affinity.

kim: ops runbook edits: add a step to pause randomized-drain when bulk-eviction-detected alert fires, and set a dashboard with fragmentation metric (percent of leases < 8GB).

raj: one more thing — cost note: scattered replicas increase inter-AZ egress which we bill ~0.02 USD/GB. last night was ~1.2TB cross-az traffic from reschedules (~$24). not catastrophic but noisy and will add up.

marco: action items I can pick up: 1) PR to randomized-drain to add per-AZ semaphore + cooldown (small change), 2) implement pause hook when oncall-bot bulk-eviction alert fires, 3) file allocator ticket for lease coalescing + TTL revert.

sasha: I'll take the autoscaler scale-down change and the soft-affinity proposal. will test in staging tomorrow.

elin: I'll add sticky-shard soft-affinity to the model-serving chart and mock checkpoint warmup to measure latency improvement.

kim: I'll update runbook + fragmentation dashboard.

marco: cool. follow-ups pinned in #infra-ops board. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
